fields.description:
## Context
Gerrit Verify remains variable and macOS is usually the completion critical path, while Ubuntu cells consume contentious runner capacity. Existing duration logs identify individual tests and fixtures over one second, but there is no current exhaustive audit mapping every such cost to its unique reachable failure mode, faster overlapping coverage, prior ticket decisions, and safe remediation options. This is analysis only: preserve real E2E/integration seams and do not infer that a slow test is redundant from duration alone.

## Run-selection protocol
- CI sample: the three most recent successful non-docs-only Gerrit Verify runs completed within the prior seven days that contain all four pytest cells (Ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 and macOS 3.13). Record the exact run ids, tested SHAs, completion timestamps, cells, and any ancestry caveat in the report. If fewer than three qualify, extend the window to fourteen days and record why.
- CI logs use `--durations=25`, so they expose only each invocation's top 25 phases. Treat them as the platform/run-variation sample, not a complete census below rank 25.
- Completeness pass: on current `origin/main`, run the exact macOS-shaped default and integration selectors once with the workflow worker/distribution settings and `--durations=0 --durations-min=1.0`, no coverage tracing, to enumerate every locally observed setup/call/teardown phase at or above 1.0s. Record command, SHA, interpreter, host, and timestamp. Do not create a CI dispatch.
- Inventory union: all >=1.0s phases from the local completeness pass plus every >=1.0s phase visible in the selected CI top-25 logs. Explicitly state that a CI-only phase below rank 25 remains unobservable and is a measurement limitation.

## Plan
- Build the normalized inventory under the run-selection protocol, retaining node id, phase, duration, platform/Python cell, run id or local provenance, and family.
- Group parameterized nodes and coherent fixture families, inspect their production/test paths, and identify the unique failure mode or contract each reaches plus any faster overlapping tests.
- For each possible removal, refactor, sample, static corpus, fixture-scope, or tier move, search ticket titles/descriptions/comments/history for prior bugs, rejected approaches, blind spots, and accepted precedents.
- Compare safe proposals with popular actively maintained OSS practice when it materially informs fidelity and record the named projects/workflow or test references.
- Quantify expected per-cell wall and aggregate runner savings, distinguishing macOS critical-path impact from Ubuntu contention and labeling xdist/host-variance uncertainty.
- Produce evidence-backed keep/refactor/move recommendations and ranked next actions without changing code, tests, workflows, or CI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The report identifies the three CI runs selected by the stated protocol.
- [x] The report records each selected run's id, tested SHA, completion time, and all four pytest cells.
- [x] The local completeness commands and execution provenance are recorded.
- [x] The inventory contains every >=1.0s phase emitted by the local completeness pass.
- [x] The inventory contains every >=1.0s phase visible in the selected CI top-25 reports.
- [x] The report states the CI top-25 truncation limitation and does not claim completeness for unreported CI phases.
- [x] Every inventoried node or coherent family has a keep, refactor, or move recommendation.
- [x] Every inventoried node or coherent family cites its unique failure mode or coverage rationale.
- [x] Every optimization proposal cites relevant tracker aliases/ids and statuses.
- [x] Every proposal records any prior rejection, gotcha, or coverage blind spot found.
- [x] Real external, process, filesystem, concurrency, packaging, and platform seams are retained when mocks cannot provide equivalent confidence.
- [x] Each proposal reports projected macOS wall-clock impact.
- [x] Each proposal reports projected Ubuntu and total runner impact.
- [x] Summed xdist phase-seconds are not reported as additive wall time.
- [x] Measurement gaps and confidence are explicit.
- [x] Each OSS-backed proposal names the maintained projects and cites the inspected workflow or test references.
- [x] Ranked next actions are recorded on this ticket.
- [x] No repository file, workflow, test, CI dispatch, or push was performed; only prescribed tracker writebacks and this audit's closure were performed under the operator's later completion instruction.
